content: Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid are indicated for colon cleansing as a preparation for colonoscopy in adults. The preparation requires two doses, which can be administered either as a split-dose regimen or as a day-before regimen. For the product Prepopik, one dose is prepared by dissolving the contents of one packet in 5 ounces of cold water using the provided measuring cup. For Clenpiq, one dose is provided as a ready-to-drink solution in a 160 mL bottle. Patients should be instructed to consume only clear liquids throughout the day before the colonoscopy and on the day of the procedure until two hours prior to the colonoscopy. All fluid intake should be stopped at least two hours before the procedure. Solid foods, dairy products, and beverages that are red or purple in color should be avoided. Alcohol consumption is also prohibited. The safety and efficacy of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid have been established for patients aged 9 years and older. However, these parameters have not been established for patients under 9 years of age. Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid can decrease the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction may reduce the absorption of baloxavir marboxil. Studies in monkeys have shown that concurrent use with calcium, aluminum, or iron significantly decreases plasma levels of baloxavir marboxil, though human studies have not been conducted. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Acetohydroxamic acid may reduce the effects of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid by altering their metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration of antibiotics, such as amikacin, amoxicillin, ampicillin, azithromycin, aztreonam, cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftaroline, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, ceftriaxone, and cefuroxime, can decrease the efficacy of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid. This occurs because antibiotics alter the colonic bacterial flora required to convert sodium picosulfate into its active form. Caution and monitoring are recommended when these drugs are used together. Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid may increase the toxicity of aspirin, aspirin rectal, aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate, celecoxib, and choline magnesium trisalicylate. These combinations may be associated with fluid and electrolyte imbalances, such as hypokalemia. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid can decrease the levels of carbonyl iron, chlorpromazine, demeclocycline, and ciprofloxacin due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. To avoid magnesium chelation, these medications should be taken at least two hours before or not less than six hours after the administration of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid. Dexamethasone, betamethasone, cortisone, and corticotropin may increase the toxicity of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid. These combinations may lead to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, including hypokalemia. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Dapsone, clindamycin, clarithromycin, clofazimine, colistin, cycloserine, and daptomycin may reduce the effects of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid by altering their metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Deflazacort and sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Diclofenac and sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid may increase each other's toxicity. This combination may be associated with fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Caution and monitoring are advised.
